bullets.title: Peak earnings week: MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, INTC plus FOMC Wednesday
bullets.body: ~46% of S&P market cap reports this week including MSFT (Wed AH, cons $4.71 EPS), GOOGL (Wed AH, $3.03), AMZN (Thu AH, $1.97), and INTC (Thu AH). FOMC widely expected to hold Wednesday; GS/MS see final hike coming in December with 2 more total. Options imply ~10% avg move on megacap tech prints, near 10-year highs, while MSFT implied vol at 4% looks cheap vs 8Q avg of 7%.

bullets.title: META $95B equity raise dominates tape; NVDA/AMD/AVGO as $5B cornerstone buyers
bullets.body: META launched $22.5B Class A common + $12.5B mandatory convertible preferred (pricing Oct 26 post-close) plus plans a separate $60B ATM program in Class C stock starting Q1 2027, totaling ~$95B. NVDA, AMD, and AVGO each indicated up to $5B interest in Class A shares; META trades up ~1-2% pre-market as overhang seen as resolving. META expects $135-145B capex in 2026 funded via operating cash flow, IG debt, and this equity raise.

bullets.title: Neocloud financing seized up; Musk warns 200+ face 'guppy-level death'
bullets.body: Debt markets have "almost entirely shut off" access for AI datacenter-only companies per Musk/GS commentary. SpaceX closed a $40B debt deal (IG-rated, diversified revenue) but CoreWeave CDS surged to record 266bp and neoclouds broadly sold off. GS Prime saw ~$20B TMT net selling over two weeks approaching July AI unwind levels; risk appetite indicator at lowest since April 2025. CRWV -2.4%, IREN -1.9%, BTDR -1.9% pre-market Monday.

bullets.title: Semis down >30% from highs; market pricing ~25-30% cuts to 2028 compute—UBS sees value
bullets.body: SOX fell ~3.2% last week and is down 18.5% from early October highs; 25% of semi names screen oversold on 14-day RSI, most since April 2025. UBS argues the market is discounting 25-30% cuts to 2028 compute vs. the 70GW supply chain estimate, calling current SMH valuation at 10-year median 21x attractive. Three overhangs: land/power/shell gap (~20-25GW), neocloud financing, and open-model concentration risk. Hedge funds de-grossed AI Mon-Thu then partially re-grossed hyperscalers Friday.

bullets.title: Core inflation poised to run ~30bp above Fed forecast; year-end risk rising
bullets.body: 22V warns core inflation could surprise 30bp/month above the Fed's path as tariff refund windowns, AI-driven electronics price pressures, war broadening, and annual price resets compound. With unemployment claims at the 0.1 percentile historically and the labor market in 'low hire/low fire' mode, the Fed is unlikely to tolerate an overshoot—tightening financial conditions risk increases. Base case: 2 more hikes (December, March) needed; flatter yield curves expected from questioned 2028+ AI capex plus near-term hot inflation.

bullets.title: 10-year yield breaches 5%; 2-year at 4.71%—cross-asset stress spreading
bullets.body: The 10-year UST broke through 5% to the downside (now ~5.00%) with the 2-year at 4.707% (+2.5bp). JPM fixed income strategy recommends holding 10s/30s steepeners and sees yields moving modestly higher near-term. Data center SASB bonds continue to widen as AI angst enters credit markets; HY spreads (+63bp in 1 month) show stress concentrated in AI/tech issuers while IG spreads remain range-bound. LQD flipped from Neutral to Bearish per Hedgeye risk ranges.

bullets.title: Brazil Lula election win triggers EM selloff; JPM downgrades to underweight
bullets.body: Lula's victory defied 75% prediction-market odds favoring Bolsonaro; JPM immediately downgraded Brazil equity to underweight, forecasting Ibovespa PE compression from 9.7x to 7x (-28%) and ~20% index decline with circuit breaker risk. USD/BRL target moved to 5.50 (10% BRL depreciation); sovereign credit downgraded from market-weight to underweight. Brazilian ADRs already pricing damage: XP -47.4%, PAGS -31.9%. WTI also fell 2.17% on risk-off.

bullets.title: AI capex ROI debate escalating: hyperscalers vs. neoclouds bifurcating sharply
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley argues top-4 hyperscalers (GOOGL, AMZN, META, MSFT) can sustain 50%+ capex growth in 2027 targeting 25%+ ROIC, given AA ratings and ample debt capacity. In contrast, lower-quality AI players face constrained unsecured access; credit markets are differentiating sharply. 22V pegs revenue per GW at $30-50B vs compute costs of $40-50B/GW, directly threatening neocloud margin viability. Enterprise AI adoption remains below VC spending, with mainstream corporates reluctant to pay for frontier models.

bullets.title: UBS raises server CPU TAM to $210B by 2030; memory supply is binding constraint, MU best play
bullets.body: UBS lifted its C2030 server CPU TAM from $175B to $210B on higher head-node and standalone AI CPU units, but notes unconstrained demand could exceed $500B—DRAM shortage is the binding limit. Ideal CPU-to-GPU ratio for AI settling at 3:1-4:1; AI CPUs need ~1.5TB memory vs 0.5TB for traditional CPUs. MU is preferred over AMD/INTC as the purest memory-demand play; demand upside is also positive for ABF substrates, TSMC, PCBs, and semicap.

bullets.title: Midterm macro setup: semiconductors and software historically outperform post-midterms
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes tariffs and executive policy are immune to midterm outcomes, but fiscal policy, data-center state-level permitting (TX, OH, PA, GA governor races), and bank M&A approvals are all in play. Stocks historically rally post-midterms led by semis and software. Republican sweep = upside risk to Treasury supply and USD; narrow Democratic majority increases gridlock risk, pressuring long-end yields. Democrats favored 88%/60% for House/Senate per 22V.

bullets.title: HF deleveraging approaching exhaustion—but alpha generation worst stretch since GFC
bullets.body: Goldman's HF VIP basket gave back ~50% of post-ChatGPT gains; L/S 20-day alpha at -2.9%, worst since Feb 2021. US L/S net exposure hit the 0th percentile on a 5-year lookback with $20B TMT net selling. Positioning breadth vs. price gap is second widest since 1990. Multiple strategists (JPM, GS, Citi) characterize this as a pure deleveraging episode where stops matter more than value—and estimate it is in final innings, creating potential for violent positioning spikes.

bullets.title: Sector rotation underway: Software outperforming Semis; Capital Goods deteriorating
bullets.body: Oppenheimer downgrades semis to Market Weight after 200-day average broke; software participation improved from 65% to 82% since August while semis collapsed from 88% to 26%. Commercial Services and Insurance upgraded to overweight. S&P ex-AI index now outperforming S&P 500 YTD; S&P 500 breadth improved to 60% above 200-day MA (best monthly improvement in 3 years) but headline flat due to concentration. Capital goods names (VRT, GEV) widely flagged as sell-into-strength.

bullets.title: AWS capacity sold out through 2027; Amazon scaling seasonal hires to 300K
bullets.body: Amazon CEO Jassy confirmed AWS 2026 capacity is sold out, most large capacity blocks for 2027 are booked, and meaningful share of 2028 is already committed—the strongest demand signal ahead of Thursday's print. VZ simultaneously announced a $2B+ AWS deal for distributed AI compute. Separately, AMZN is raising holiday seasonal hires to 300K (from 250K) signaling elevated demand expectations.

bullets.title: US housing at multi-year lows: NAHB HMI hits 14-year trough of 29
bullets.body: 30-year mortgage rates fell 8bp to 7.32% but demand failed to respond: pending sales dropped to -14.4% YoY (worst since June 2023), purchase applications at -15.7% on 4-week MA (worst since April 2024), and NAHB HMI fell to 29—below the April 2020 pandemic trough of 30. Single-family permits fell to 845K, lowest since March 2023. Mortgage rates remain 113bp above year-ago levels despite weekly relief.

bullets.title: AI power trade technically broken; Hedgeye shorts GEV, CMI on peak-order risk
bullets.body: Hedgeye moves GE Vernova to active short and Cummins to top short, arguing 'sold out through 2030' signals peak orders and margin risk rather than a bull thesis. 70% of 20 AI power/infrastructure stocks have poor technical scores; 100% are below their 50-day MAs and 75% below 200-day MAs. Competitors entering market (Ansaldo, CAT, CMI doubling engine capacity); fixed-price contracts and policy headwinds (~70% Dem sweep probability) add further pressure. Energy and healthcare names show 95% with good/strong technicals by contrast.

bullets.title: Token usage exploding but neocloud financing stress threatens hyperscaler capex conviction
bullets.body: JPM data shows token spend growth accelerated +40% MoM in October driven by premium model mix (Opus 5.5); H100 GPU rental up 6.5% MoM, B200 up 4.7% MoM even as A100 fell 3.5%. But the debate is shifting from demand to financing: SpaceX CDS at record 266bp, CoreWeave bonds yield ~15%, and Ramp data shows 80% of Anthropic/OpenAI spend concentrated in top 1% of enterprises (mostly VC-backed), creating fragility if VC funding falters.

bullets.title: Starlink 80K tower deal poses structural threat to telecom sector multiples
bullets.body: SpaceX reportedly securing 80K+ US cell sites (likely Crown Castle) to support low-band spectrum strategy; theoretical Starlink upper limit revised to ~24M US phones served. Wolfe rates T Outperform but sees structural 4th-carrier risk from Starlink depressing sector multiples; telecom bounces should be sold. Separately, Starlink mobile service expected to turn on early 2028, faster than market expected. T fell 10% and TMUS fell 8% on Starlink mobile news.

bullets.title: Global growth resilient but skewed to downside; oil near $100 adds inflation pressure
bullets.body: JPM Global Data Watch: China 3Q26 GDP at 4.6% ar beat expectations; global headline CPI forecast at 4% ar this quarter on oil up ~30% from last quarter's average. US consumer spending expected to cool to 1.5% ar this quarter. Fed, ECB, BoJ all expected to hold next week but single hikes coming. German IFO edged up 0.3pt to 90.2 in October; Japan semis stocks down 26% on AI infrastructure sustainability concerns and oil above $100.

bullets.title: Software M&A accelerating: $40B+ in October deals; cybersecurity stocks rally on PHP2Shell
bullets.body: Five major software M&A deals in October totaling >$40B include Schneider/PTC ($24B), Salesforce/Braze (~$6B), and Proofpoint/Varonis; average deal EV/NTM Sales ~7.2x. AI-identified PHP2Shell vulnerability sparked a cybersecurity rally: Zscaler +15%, Check Point +10%, Okta +8%. MS expects bank M&A to accelerate through 2027-28 under faster regulatory approvals and capital rule relief post-midterms.

bullets.title: AI capex bifurcation: factory construction set to accelerate even as tech capex moderates
bullets.body: PSC Macro argues AI/tech capex slows to 35-50% YoY in 2027 vs 60-80% in 2026, but factory/manufacturing construction accelerates as Fed easing, easier bank lending, and reshoring incentives kick in. ABI C&I index moved above 50% in September; S&P Manufacturing PMI at 56.0 in October. Dodge nonresidential starts +16% YoY in September driven by data center buildings (+69% YoY). AI's net contribution to US demand is ~50-60bp, not the 100bp+ commonly cited per 22V.
